answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust earned over time, not claimed at signup: each identity starts with a tiny spending cap that only grows as it completes real jobs and settles disputes, like rings in cedar that appear only with age. Clones cannot flood a vote, since every newcomer must first do checkable work, and a prism of independent reviewers with no shared operator must agree it was genuine. A proven record becomes an oasis others trust; clones stay stranded.
